---
title: "Probability & Sampling"
subtitle: "Probability theory, random sampling, and sampling variability."
---

::: {.callout-note title="Where you are in your learning journey" icon=false}
**Where you come from.** You arrive here from [Means & Variance](means-and-variance.qmd). You can describe a variable with its mean and spread.

**What this module adds.** You'll learn the basics of probability, random sampling, probability distributions (especially the normal distribution), and why samples differ from the population.

**Why it is valuable.** This explains why we can learn about a population from a sample, and why every result comes with uncertainty. That idea is the foundation of hypothesis testing.

**Where it leads.** Next up: [Effects](effects.qmd).
:::

## Planned content

- Probability basics and simulation with `sample()` / `rnorm()`
- Populations, samples, and random sampling
- The normal distribution (and the z-score) as a model for variables
- Sampling variability: the sampling distribution of the mean and the standard error
